Step 1: the dark bluish gray 2x6 plate (b1) is the first piece of the model, so it rests on nothing.

Step 2: the plate is turned upside down. Each light bluish gray round 2x2 plate (b2, b3) goes on the underside, with its studs in the anti-studs of the 2x6 plate. b2 is already placed at the left end in the picture, and b3 is the one being added at the right end.
Each round plate covers 4 anti-studs, at columns 1-2 for b2 and columns 5-6 for b3. I listed one representative port pair per join.
The round plates' axle holes are open and will take the wheel axles on a later page.

Step 3: the model is still upside down. Each black 2x2 wheel-holder plate (b4, b5) goes onto the round plate at its end of the 2x6 plate. b4 is already in place at the left end in the picture, and b5 is the one being added at the right end.

The wheel holders' studs go into the anti-studs of the round plates (b2, b3), so each holder rests only on its round plate. The round plate covers the same 2x2 footprint, so the holder does not touch b1.
The wheel-holder pins are free for the wheels on a later page.
Step 4 has no arrows, only a picture of the result. The model is now turned right side up, and the 2x6 plate b1 faces up with its studs.

The picture shows 2x2 blocks of studs at each end of b1. I read each end as a side-handle plate (b6 or b8) at the outermost column plus a 1x2 plate (b7 or b9) in the next column. The parts list has exactly 2x lego-2540 and 2x lego-3023, which matches this reading.
The side-handle bars point outward at the ends. Both bars rest on b1 and are shown with a pair of anti-stud to stud joins.
The exact placement is a guess from a small image, and it could be the other way round, with the 1x2 plate at the outer column.
The four middle studs of b1 (columns 3-4) stay uncovered. The black wheel holders and round plates are now underneath.
Step 5: two orange mudguards go on the 2x2 stud blocks at the ends. b10 is already on the left end in the picture, and b11 is being added at the right end.
Each mudguard sits on the 2x2 block made of a side-handle plate and a 1x2 plate: b10 on b6 and b7, b11 on b8 and b9. The 2x6 plate b1 is covered underneath, so I do not list it as clutched.
The side-handle bars still stick out past the mudguards at the ends.
The mudguard's anti-stud ports (middle columns 2-3) are an assumed mapping, since the mudguard is 4 long and covers only a 2x2 stud area.
Step 6 has no sub-assembly box. The picture shows some pieces already placed and one being added.
Left mudguard b10: two white jumper plates (b12, b13) sit side by side on its 2x2 studs. They are shown already placed in the picture.

Right mudguard b11: a white grille tile (b14) covers one pair of studs, and the arrows add a white jumper plate (b15) on the other pair. This uses all 3 jumpers and the single grille tile from the parts list.
Which row each piece takes is a guess from a small image.

Step 7 has no arrows, only the result. It adds a trans-yellow cheese slope (b16) on the white jumper plate at the left mudguard. Of the two jumpers there, b12 is my guess for the one it sits on, since a jumper has a single stud.
It also adds a dark bluish gray 1x1 clip tile (b17) on a middle stud of the 2x6 plate b1, next to the left mudguard. Its clip is free for a later part such as the handlebars.
The model is rotated in this view. The slope and clip tile positions are best guesses from a small image.

Step 8 has an inset showing the blue flag (b19) clipped onto the light bluish gray antenna (b18). The antenna is then pushed onto the stud of the white jumper b15 at the right end, the end with the grille tile.
The handlebars (b20) are pushed onto the clip of the clip tile b17, next to the cheese slope. The arrow points down onto the clip.
The antenna has no bar port in the catalogue, so the flag-to-antenna clip join has no port on the antenna side.
The flag join is recorded as revolute because the flag can swivel on its clips. This is an assumption.

Step 9: the inset shows a white wheel pressed into a black tyre, built 4 times. Each wheel and tyre pair is then pushed onto one of the 4 wheel-holder pins, two on each black wheel-holder plate (b4 and b5). This gives the finished quad bike.
The 4600 holder's pins are named axle-hole.1 and axle-hole.2 in the catalogue, so I used those port names for the wheel join. The wheels turn freely, so the join is revolute.
The tyre has no ports, so the wheel-to-tyre joins have no port names.
